note: Unique strings requiring translation. Node/parameter/group names are technical identifiers and may be kept in English where a translation would obscure the correspondence with Gaea; their descriptions should be translated.

nodeDescriptions.AO: Creates an ambient occlusion map that darkens recessed areas and enhances terrain depth.
nodeDescriptions.Accumulator: Accumulates specific map types such as Water, Forest, or Snow from all available nodes.
nodeDescriptions.Adjust: The Fx node makes that process easier by combining all the common adjustments inside a single node and allowing you to toggle them on and off.
nodeDescriptions.Anastomosis: Anastomosis creates interconnected water flow based extractions, ranging from small pits to large river channels. It is useful for both terrains and textures.
nodeDescriptions.Angle: Angle creates a selection mask covering all areas of the heightfield facing the specified range.
nodeDescriptions.Aperture: Aperture expands or compacts every feature on the terrain, similar to a camera's bokeh.
nodeDescriptions.Autolevel: Automatically remaps the input to use the full available height or mask range.
nodeDescriptions.BlobRemover: BlobRemover can remove smaller fragments or blobs near larger shapes. This is very useful for cleanup.
nodeDescriptions.Blur: Blur diffuses sharp shapes and softens the terrain.
nodeDescriptions.Bomber: Bomber takes an input heightfield and "stamps" or bombs it across the entire terrain surface using the randomization properties you set.
nodeDescriptions.Bulbous: Bulbous inflates existing shapes to make them more voluminous while respecting standard geological boundaries.
nodeDescriptions.CLUTer: CLUTer creates color gradients which can be mapped to texture masks to make color maps.
nodeDescriptions.Canyon: Canyon is a simple, fast, and detailed canyon primitive. It creates a drainage based river canyon.
nodeDescriptions.Cartography: Cartography creates a topographical overlay for a map.
nodeDescriptions.Cellular: Cellular creates cell-based patterns and noises that can be quite versatile as they're ever-present in nature.
nodeDescriptions.Cellular3D: Generates three-dimensional cellular noise useful for volumetric-looking patterns and complex terrain breakup.
nodeDescriptions.Chokepoint: Chokepoint node is a special node whose sole purpose is to help avoid re-connecting many nodes, while adding no memory overhead.
nodeDescriptions.Clamp: Clamp controls the height of the terrain. You can squash the terrain, clip it at certain heights, or make it taller using the Extend operation.
nodeDescriptions.Clip: Cuts the terrain against a threshold, removing values above or below a specified level.
nodeDescriptions.ColorErosion: Applies erosion-style transport and deposition to color data, creating more natural weathered color variation.
nodeDescriptions.ColorThreshold: Creates a greyscale mask from a specified color range.
nodeDescriptions.Combine: Combine is one of Gaea's most important nodes. You can combine two terrains (or any node output) using various mathematical operations often known as Blend Modes.
nodeDescriptions.Compare: Compares two inputs and produces a result based on their relative values.
nodeDescriptions.Cone: Generates a simple conical gradient that is useful as a primitive shape or mask.
nodeDescriptions.Constant: Constant creates a blank terrain of the height specified, or a flat color output.
nodeDescriptions.Contours: Creates map-like contours for a terrain. Useful for making maps or for other overlays.
nodeDescriptions.Cracks: Cracks primitive creates large, cracked patterns on a flat base.
nodeDescriptions.Craggy: Turns a terrain's surface into a craggy, rocky, broken landscape.
nodeDescriptions.Crater: Crater primitive creates different types of crater shapes.
nodeDescriptions.CraterField: Creates a landscape full of craters.
nodeDescriptions.Crumble: Crumble runs a different kind of simulation that feeds off of existing crevices, erosive information, and other subtle details to collapse the terrain. Just as the name implies, the terrain starts crumbling from the edges.
nodeDescriptions.Curvature: Curvature creates a mask where convex areas (protrusions, sharp edges, etc.) are selected. Very useful layer in texture creation, often as highlights on top of an existing texture map.
nodeDescriptions.Curve: Curve adjusts the height curve of a terrain.
nodeDescriptions.DataExtractor: Extracts specific derived data such as boundaries, differences, or Modifier maps from an input.
nodeDescriptions.Debris: Simulates loose debris across the terrain surface to create broken rocky accumulation.
nodeDescriptions.Deflate: Compresses and pulls terrain features inward, reducing bulk and prominence.
nodeDescriptions.Denoise: Denoise is a general purpose noise removal filter that systematically cleans up random noise, spikes, and extremely sharp edges.
nodeDescriptions.Dilate: Dilate the pixels of the heightfield or mask.
nodeDescriptions.DirectionalWarp: DWarp or Directional Warp uses a secondary input to warp the first input in a uniform direction.
nodeDescriptions.Distance: Generates a distance field from the input, measuring how far each point is from the nearest boundary or feature.
nodeDescriptions.Distress: Adds superficial wear, breakup, and irregular damage to a surface.
nodeDescriptions.DotNoise: Generates dotted or speckled noise patterns for texturing and breakup.
nodeDescriptions.Draw: Draw draws entire mountain ranges in the shape you choose.
nodeDescriptions.DriftNoise: DriftNoise is a unique primitive that can create overlapping "shelves". It is a versatile primitive noise that can be used in various scenarios from cliffs to crack production.
nodeDescriptions.DuneSea: Creates broad fields of dune-like terrain suitable for deserts and wind-shaped landscapes.
nodeDescriptions.Dusting: Applies a thin dusting of snow or sediment over the terrain surface.
nodeDescriptions.EasyErosion: Provides a simplified erosion workflow for quickly adding natural erosion effects.
nodeDescriptions.Edge: Zero Borders softly transitions the edges of a terrain into nothing, similar to a vignette effect in paint applications. Useful when using Bomber or other effects where a tall edge would be problematic.
nodeDescriptions.Equalize: Redistributes the input values to balance the histogram and reveal more detail across the range.
nodeDescriptions.Erosion: Erosion is the cornerstone of all terrains. It simulates hydraulic erosion and turns any shape into a realistic-looking terrain.
nodeDescriptions.Erosion2: An advanced hydraulic erosion node that creates more detailed and realistic erosion results.
nodeDescriptions.Export: Exports terrain, masks, or textures to external files.
nodeDescriptions.Extend: Expands the terrain range beyond its current limits, effectively stretching elevation values.
nodeDescriptions.File: File loads any supported image or data file as a terrain, and supports all major file formats. You can also transform the input.
nodeDescriptions.Filter: Applies profile-based filtering to reshape terrain values and refine feature response.
nodeDescriptions.Flip: Flip flips the terrain horizontally, vertically, or both.
nodeDescriptions.FlowMap: Generates a modern flow map showing how water or material would travel across the terrain.
nodeDescriptions.FlowMapClassic: Generates a classic-style flow map based on legacy flow behavior.
nodeDescriptions.Fold: Fold simulates terrain folding by introducing slants, breaks, and folds to the terrain. It significantly changes the terrain shape and should be used early in the graph.
nodeDescriptions.FractalTerraces: FractalTerraces creates fractal terracing on the terrain. It is a powerful alternative to the Terrace node.
nodeDescriptions.Gabor: Gabor noise is one of the lesser used noises, but provides a wonderful pattern-friendly noise that can be used to simulate various aspects of nature.
nodeDescriptions.Gamma: Gamma applies Gamma adjustment to the heightfield, working exactly like Gamma in an image processing program.
nodeDescriptions.Gate: Defines a baking boundary for the graph by forcing all ancestor nodes to be baked.
nodeDescriptions.Glacier: Glacier creates flowing glaciers on mountain tops.
nodeDescriptions.GraphicEQ: Reshapes terrain using multiple adjustable bands, similar to an equalizer for height profiles.
nodeDescriptions.Grid: Generates a regular grid pattern useful for cartography, masking, or stylized surfaces.
nodeDescriptions.GroundTexture: GroundTexture adds superficial detail to the terrain to increase realism.
nodeDescriptions.HSL: Adjusts the hue, saturation, and lightness of a color input.
nodeDescriptions.Halftone: Converts the terrain or mask into a halftone-style rendered output.
nodeDescriptions.Heal: Heal reconstructs damaged, low res, or 8-bit data with 16-bit, high resolution fidelity. It cleans up quantized images with extreme banding of any shape, and yields naturalistic terrain output.
nodeDescriptions.Height: Height creates a selection mask within the height range specified.
nodeDescriptions.Hemisphere: Generates a hemispherical gradient useful for domes, mounds, and radial falloffs.
nodeDescriptions.Hillify: Softens and reshapes terrain into smoother, hill-like forms.
nodeDescriptions.HydroFix: HydroFix alters the terrain to create continuous drainage network friendly slopes. It can be used before Erosion or other flow related nodes to get better results.
nodeDescriptions.IceFloe: Icefloe creates flat plates of ice inside a water body.
nodeDescriptions.Island: Island draws basic shapes from which entire landmasses can be generated.
nodeDescriptions.Lake: Lake simulates rainfall on the terrain and creates physically accurate lakes.
nodeDescriptions.Layers: Combines multiple layers using blend operations in a stacked workflow.
nodeDescriptions.Lichtenberg: Creates branching, lightning-like erosion or fracture patterns.
nodeDescriptions.LightX: Creates a fully lit render using controllable sun, shadow, and ambient lighting.
nodeDescriptions.LineNoise: LineNoise is a geometry generator that creates sets of lines which can be distorted and used with other noises and fractals to produce layered ridges.
nodeDescriptions.LinearGradient: Generates a straight linear gradient across the terrain.
nodeDescriptions.MacroPort: Defines an input or output port inside a macro for passing height, mask, or color data.
nodeDescriptions.Mask: Mask draws a mask. If the Input port is connected to another node, a 2D representation of that terrain is shown in the background as a guide. This is optional, as the Input port only provides a drawing guide and does not affect the actual mask.
nodeDescriptions.Match: Matches the height range or histogram of one terrain to another.
nodeDescriptions.MathX: Evaluates mathematical expressions to generate or modify terrain data procedurally.
nodeDescriptions.Median: Applies a median filter to remove spikes, speckles, and small noise while preserving edges better than blur.
nodeDescriptions.Mesher: Mesher can save specific nodes as meshes instead of heightfields, and can also generate LODs.
nodeDescriptions.Meshify: Converts terrain into a faceted, mesh-like surface with controllable vertex density and detail sensitivity.
nodeDescriptions.Mixer: Mixer allows layer-based manipulation of color textures and contains in-built masking.
nodeDescriptions.Mountain: Mountain is one of Gaea's most versatile primitives, using a modulated Voronoi pattern and distortions to create realistic mountain shapes, ready for further modification and erosion.
nodeDescriptions.MountainRange: Range primitive quickly sets up an entire mountain terrain with shapes highly optimized for eroding large-scale landscapes.
nodeDescriptions.MountainSide: Generates a single mountain slope or mountainside formation.
nodeDescriptions.MultiFractal: MultiFractal creates a multi-noise that can have a large level of variations. Often useful for texturing.
nodeDescriptions.Noise: Noise applies controlled single-pixel noise onto the terrain.
nodeDescriptions.Normals: Generates a normal map from the terrain for shading and downstream workflows.
nodeDescriptions.Object: Loads external object or mesh data for use inside the graph.
nodeDescriptions.Occlusion: Occlusion behaves similarly to Ambient Occlusion, but favors sedimentary processes vs. lighting.
nodeDescriptions.Origami: Origami creates a diagonal multifold pattern, and can produce a highly stylized terrain.
nodeDescriptions.Outcrops: The Outcrops LookDev node creates rocky outcrops on any surface. You can control coverage, breakage, and surface details. Several Outcrops nodes can be layered for complex results.
nodeDescriptions.Pattern: Generates repeatable geometric or decorative patterns for masking and stylized terrain work.
nodeDescriptions.Peaks: Creates a mask that isolates the peaks and highest protruding parts of the terrain.
nodeDescriptions.Perlin: Perlin is the most basic and essential noise. In Gaea, we've made a "geo-variant" by modifying the base Perlin shape to fit the needs of terrain design from the beginning.
nodeDescriptions.Pixelate: Converts the input into a blocky, pixelated version.
nodeDescriptions.Plates: Plates primitive is based on a Perlin core with flat plate-like formations created in between larger Perlin-esque shapes.
nodeDescriptions.Pockmarks: Creates scattered pits, dents, and small impact-like depressions on the surface.
nodeDescriptions.PointCloud: Exports the terrain as a point cloud in formats such as PLY, XYZ, or CSV.
nodeDescriptions.RGBMerge: Combines three heightfields into a single RGB color output by packing them into separate channels.
nodeDescriptions.RGBSplit: RGBSplit takes a color node and splits the Red/Green/Blue channels into heightfields. The counterpart to RGBMix.
nodeDescriptions.RadialGradient: Generates a circular gradient radiating outward from a center point.
nodeDescriptions.Recurve: Recurve is a curvature-based expander that inflates and/or deflates the terrain to create stronger slopes and larger, softer formations from a given noise or terrain.
nodeDescriptions.Repeat: Repeat takes a shape and repeats it in a tiled pattern. It is often combined with the Seamless node.
nodeDescriptions.Reseed: Re-randomizes an upstream procedural node by overriding or refreshing its seed behavior.
nodeDescriptions.Ridge: Ridge creates a rugged ridgeline with multiple fractures and rock shearing.
nodeDescriptions.Rivers: Rivers creates a realistic network of rivers with controllable headwaters.
nodeDescriptions.RockMap: RockMap creates a rock-like coverage mask that can be used to texture terrains on its own or combined with other Data Maps.
nodeDescriptions.RockNoise: RockNoise is a useful tool for generating fields of rocks with size variations and controllable density.
nodeDescriptions.Rockscape: Creates broad rocky surface formations and broken stone-like terrain detail.
nodeDescriptions.Roughen: Adds fine roughness and small-scale breakup to the terrain surface.
nodeDescriptions.Route: Route chooses the flow of the graph based on the Input/Output ports chosen, and relies on integer input for automation.
nodeDescriptions.Rugged: Rugged is a very powerful primitive node that creates a strong, rocky surface for any terrain while preserving overall shape.
nodeDescriptions.Sand: Sand creates medium and small level sand patterns. It can also be used to simulate dunes.
nodeDescriptions.Sandstone: Creates layered sandstone-like terracing and sedimentary rock structure.
nodeDescriptions.SatMap: Generates terrain color from preset satellite-style palettes with controllable range and processing.
nodeDescriptions.Scree: Creates accumulations of loose rock fragments scattered across slopes and terrain edges.
nodeDescriptions.Sea: Sea is a multi-function water surface generator and coastal erosion tool. Its primary purpose is to create a water surface, while Coastal Erosion creates beaches and cliffs.
nodeDescriptions.Seamless: Seamless can transform any input terrain or color map into a tileable/repeating pattern.
nodeDescriptions.Sediments: Sediments creates a thick layer of generic sedimentation on top of the terrain, which can be used for sand or snow.
nodeDescriptions.Shade: Produces a shaded terrain render based on lighting direction and surface relief.
nodeDescriptions.Shape: Generates basic geometric terrain shapes for use as primitives or masks.
nodeDescriptions.Shaper: Shaper bulks up or bulks down a terrain, while optionally retaining the finer details.
nodeDescriptions.Sharpen: Sharpen enhances terrain edges and small structures by making them more prominent.
nodeDescriptions.Shatter: Shatter transforms simple shapes into complex, highly eroded, and fractured terrains.
nodeDescriptions.Shear: Shear creates rock shearing and exposes strata.
nodeDescriptions.Shrubs: Adds low vegetation or shrub-like surface growth across the terrain.
nodeDescriptions.Slope: Slope creates a selection mask within the slope range specified.
nodeDescriptions.SlopeBlur: SlopeBlur is a versatile, low-level node that adds directional blurring based on the slopes of a Guide terrain or mask. It is one of our deceptively simple nodes that can create a wide array of shapes.
nodeDescriptions.SlopeWarp: SlopeBlur is a versatile, low-level node that adds directional warping based on the slopes of a Guide terrain or mask. It behaves similarly to SlopeBlur.
nodeDescriptions.Slump: Slump is a simple primitive that creates relative smooth hills with slumped (collapsed) areas. It is very useful for creating large landscapes.
nodeDescriptions.Snow: Snow simulates snow fall, melt, and settling like in nature, and controls how the snow adheres and flows along the terrain.
nodeDescriptions.Snowfield: Creates broad settled snow coverage across the terrain surface.
nodeDescriptions.SoftClip: SoftClip a low-level utility that lets you softly reduce the intensity of shapes above a specified threshold. It can be comparable to masking a shape with a Height node and then clamping that portion.
nodeDescriptions.Soil: Soil Map creates a soil mask, with increased density in crevices or other areas where the slope allows soil to settle.
nodeDescriptions.Splat: Splat is similar to RGBMix, taking heightfield nodes and encoding them to the RGB channels of a color map, and providing properties to control the inputs.
nodeDescriptions.Steps: Creates stepped formations and hard terrace-like breaks in the terrain.
nodeDescriptions.Stones: Scatters stones or small rock forms across the surface.
nodeDescriptions.Stratify: Stratify creates broken strata or rock layers on the terrain in a non-linear fashion, producing a robust, realistic formation.
nodeDescriptions.Sunlight: Sunlight is a Data Map that gives you the sunlight integral (sun light/shadow map) of any given period (up to 365 days). It can be used to drive snow melt, vegetation growth, and more.
nodeDescriptions.SuperColor: Applies procedural terrain colorization using texture, flow, peaks, and palette controls.
nodeDescriptions.Swirl: Swirl creates a vortex warp on the terrain. Very useful for adding a fluid look.
nodeDescriptions.Switch: Switch chooses between two different heightfield inputs and relies on a boolean (true/false) input.
nodeDescriptions.Synth: Synth takes a bitmap image (photo or artwork) and converts it to CLUT map that can be used with a texture mask to colorize your terrain.
nodeDescriptions.Terraces: Creates stepped terrace formations from the terrain.
nodeDescriptions.TextureBaker: Bakes derived texture maps from the terrain for export and downstream use.
nodeDescriptions.TextureBase: Texture uses multiple factors (such as chaos, slopes, flow zones, and other geological features) to create a texture mask for any color node to create a texture map. Can be used by itself, or combined with other data maps and selectors.
nodeDescriptions.Texturizer: Generates terrain texture masks using preset styles and controllable secondary effects.
nodeDescriptions.Thermal: Thermal simulates Thermal Erosion to create talus and debris.
nodeDescriptions.Thermal2: Thermal2 is an evolution of the previous node. It creates Thermal Erosion to create realistic talus and debris.
nodeDescriptions.ThermalShaper: ThermalShaper is a fast, basic simulation of the concavity and convexity that can be achieved from thermal erosion. The effect can be exaggerated for artistic effect.
nodeDescriptions.Threshold: Abs can modify the terrain or mask it by eliminating values higher or lower than the exact value specified.
nodeDescriptions.TileInput: Reads a set of tiles for 1:1 input into a tiled build, or combines it into a single input.
nodeDescriptions.Tint: QuickColor quickly maps a 2-color gradient to any mask. Useful for simple scenarios where CLUTer would be overkill.
nodeDescriptions.Transform: Transform moves, rotates, and scales any terrain. A post-process effect, it can be implemented at any point in the graph.
nodeDescriptions.Transform3D: Applies full 3D transformation to the terrain, including rotation and spatial adjustment.
nodeDescriptions.Transpose: Adapts the terrain to the substructures of a given reference terrain.
nodeDescriptions.Trees: The Arboreal Node gives you the power of creating superficial forests and vegetation. These forests are part of the heightfield while being "detached" enough for various export scenarios.
nodeDescriptions.Unity: Exports terrain data in Unity-friendly resolutions and formats.
nodeDescriptions.Unreal: Exports terrain data in Unreal-friendly resolutions, formats, and naming conventions.
nodeDescriptions.Uplift: Creates tectonic-style uplift by raising and shaping large terrain masses.
nodeDescriptions.Var: Reads or modifies named graph variables for procedural control and automation.
nodeDescriptions.VariableBlur: Blurs the input by varying the blur amount across the surface using local data or a guide.
nodeDescriptions.Volcano: Generates a volcanic landform with a central cone and crater structure.
nodeDescriptions.Voronoi: Voronoi is a staple of procedural design and creates sharp, geometric patterns. In Gaea, we've made a "geo-variant" by modifying the base Voronoi shape to fit the needs of terrain design from the beginning.
nodeDescriptions.Warp: Warp can take the terrain and "warp" the shape creating more believable shapes or alter simple shapes into a more complex formation. It can help breakup masks too.
nodeDescriptions.WaterColor: Colorizes water bodies using palette-based shallow and deep water tones.
nodeDescriptions.WaveShine: Generates wave-like reflective or rippling patterns useful for stylized surfaces and water-like forms.
nodeDescriptions.Weathering: Creates weathered color or mask variation that simulates dirt, fading, and environmental wear.
nodeDescriptions.Whorl: Whorl applies multiple vortex-like distortions across the terrain to create large-scale warping. Very useful for creating massive landscapes without a patterning in the noise and for creating slightly surreal or alien landscapes.
nodeDescriptions.Wizard: The Erosion Wizard is a lightweight wrapper for the Erosion node. It simplifies the settings through curated presets, and provides secondary passes for additional processing.
nodeDescriptions.Wizard2: A simplified erosion wrapper that provides curated controls for shaping erosion depth, scale, and strength.

paramDescriptions: Additional metadata or notes related to the Unreal Engine export process.
Adds additional detail and features to cliffs along the coast, enhancing realism and visual interest in steep shoreline areas.
Adds additional detail to the strata or layers within the terraces, enhancing geological realism.
Adds atmospheric haze to the scene, softening distant terrain and simulating light diffusion.
Adds darker coloration to crevices, nooks, and sheltered areas of the terrain, simulating the accumulation of soil, organic matter, or moisture.
Adds details on the ridgelines.
Adds flow-based features to the texture, simulating the effect of water or material movement across the surface.
Adds jitter in coordinate/axis space before evaluation, warping the field and introducing directional wobble and boundary distortion.
Adds noise and texture variation to the snow, creating a more natural, patchy, and irregular appearance.
Adds random noise to tree placement, scattering trees across the terrain without regard to inhibition or aspect controls. Rarely used for realistic masks.
Adds randomness to the falloff rate, producing irregular or natural-looking distance gradients.
Adds restraints to the downcutting process by slowing it down when undissolved sediments accumulate. This results in a mix of deep channels and alluvial fans, depending on local conditions.
Adds slope-based weighting to the texture, favoring either steeper or flatter areas to enhance natural variation.
Adds visible geological layering or banding to the outcrops, simulating sedimentary or stratified rock formations. High values increase the distance between Strata layers.
Adjusts how many ice floes are distributed across the surface. Higher values increase the number of floes per area.
Adjusts how many outcrops are placed across the terrain. Higher values increase the number of outcrops per area.
Adjusts how many pockmarks are scattered across the terrain. Higher values increase the number of pits per area.
Adjusts how many scree stones are distributed across the surface. Higher values increase the number of stones per area.
Adjusts how many stones are scattered across the surface. Higher values increase the number of stones per area.
Adjusts how much of the terrain surface is affected by the ground texture, determining the extent of the effect.
Adjusts the amount and detail of chipping applied to the sandstone layers, affecting the roughness and realism of eroded edges.
Adjusts the amount of erosion applied to the rockscape, simulating natural weathering and smoothing of rock surfaces.
Adjusts the amount of fine surface detail on the mountain. Higher values add more texture and small-scale features to the slope.
Adjusts the brightness or opacity of land contour lines, making them more or less prominent.
Adjusts the brightness or opacity of the grid lines, making them more or less visible.
Adjusts the brightness or opacity of the subdivision lines, which are the finer lines between main contours.
Adjusts the brightness or opacity of the subdivision lines, which are the finer lines between main grid lines.
Adjusts the brightness or opacity of water contour lines, making them more or less prominent.
Adjusts the complexity of the warp, increasing the number of layers or detail in the distortion.
Adjusts the consistency of terrace edge hardness, affecting whether terrace boundaries are sharp or soft throughout.
Adjusts the consistency of terrace step heights. Higher uniformity produces evenly spaced terraces, while lower values introduce variation.
Adjusts the contrast of the wind patch effect, making the difference between calm and windy areas more or less pronounced.
Adjusts the contrast or intensity of the Voronoi pattern, amplifying or reducing the difference between cell heights.
Adjusts the directional bias of erosion and deposit formation. Low values preserve the original terrain, while high values intensify directional erosion, shaping talus deposits and terrain features.
Adjusts the exposure level, controlling the overall brightness and dynamic range of the rendered image.
Adjusts the fine detail and small-scale shaping of terraces, adding subtle variations to each step.
Adjusts the frequency or scale of the noise pattern. Higher density results in more frequent variations across the terrain.
Adjusts the height of each tile to prevent elevation buildup at tile seams, ensuring a smoother and more seamless repeat pattern.
Adjusts the height of the shape by scaling it along the Y axis independently.
Adjusts the height or intensity of the ripples, making them more or less pronounced.
Adjusts the horizontal position of the hemisphere along the X axis, allowing you to move it left or right within the terrain.
Adjusts the horizontal position of the hemisphere along the Y axis, allowing you to move it forward or backward within the terrain.
Adjusts the hue of the gradient colors, allowing for global color shifts across the entire gradient.
Adjusts the hue of the input, shifting colors around the color wheel. Changing this value alters the overall color tone.
Adjusts the intensity of direct sunlight in the scene, affecting brightness and shadow contrast.
Adjusts the level of detail in the crack network. Higher values produce more branches and finer crack structures.
Adjusts the likelihood of generating larger or smaller lakes, influencing the overall distribution of lake sizes.
Adjusts the overall amount of snow applied to the terrain, increasing or decreasing the extent of dusting.
Adjusts the overall depth of the collapsed areas, determining how far the terrain sinks or breaks away.
Adjusts the overall hue of the weathered terrain, allowing for color shifts to match desired environmental conditions.
Adjusts the overall intensity of the weathering effect. Higher values produce more pronounced weathering.
Adjusts the overall intensity or brightness of direct sunlight in the shading calculation.
Adjusts the overall strength of the clipping effect, determining how much values are compressed toward the threshold.
Adjusts the overall strength of the sandstone effect, influencing how pronounced the layers and erosion features appear.
Adjusts the overall strength of the stratification effect, making the layers more or less pronounced.
Adjusts the ozone level in the atmosphere, influencing the color and intensity of sunlight.
Adjusts the precision of contour line placement. Higher accuracy produces more exact lines that closely follow the terrain's elevation.
Adjusts the randomness and disorder in the texture, increasing natural variation and reducing uniformity.
Adjusts the randomness or complexity of the Gabor noise. Higher entropy values result in more chaotic and less predictable patterns.
Adjusts the resolution or granularity of the pattern, controlling how fine or coarse the pattern details appear.
Adjusts the scale of features relative to the terrain size, allowing for proportional detail regardless of resolution.
Adjusts the scale of the cellular pattern along the X axis, stretching or compressing cells horizontally.
Adjusts the scale of the cellular pattern along the Y axis, stretching or compressing cells vertically.
Adjusts the scale of the cellular pattern along the Z axis, stretching or compressing cells in depth.
Adjusts the scale of thermal erosion features in meters. Larger values create broader, more pronounced features, while smaller values result in finer details.
Adjusts the scaling factor for the terrain, affecting how snow features are distributed and visualized.
Adjusts the shaping style of the terrain. Negative values condense the terrain into sharp, concise ridges, while positive values bulk up the terrain, creating softer, more rounded features.
Adjusts the simulation to favor certain environmental conditions or behaviors, influencing shrub distribution.
Adjusts the smoothness of the edge transition. Higher values result in a more gradual, blended edge.
Adjusts the smoothness of the variation, with higher values producing gentler transitions and lower values creating sharper changes.
Adjusts the strength of secondary effects such as soil accumulation, flow streaks, and breakup patterns. Use to fine-tune the complexity and realism of the texture.
Adjusts the variation in elevation or intensity between different plates, affecting the contrast and diversity of the generated regions.
Adjusts the width of the shape by scaling it along the X axis independently.
Allows custom input maps or masks to influence shrub placement and density.
Allows the dusting effect to respect and blend with existing snow layers, ensuring seamless integration.
Allows values outside the standard 0–1 range to be loaded, preserving high dynamic range or special data in the file.
Allows variations in the height of bombed instances, introducing additional randomness to their elevation.

Alters erosion physics to treat water flows as volumetric, resulting in higher water levels, wider channels, and more extensive sediment deposits. Useful for forming valley floors without downcutting.
Amount of B input channel.
Amount of G input channel.
Amount of R input channel.
Amount of alpha input channel.
Amount of boost or cut applied (used by shelf and bell modes).
An optional mathematical or logical expression to apply when modifying the variable. Used only in 'Modify' mode.
Applies Unreal Engine-compatible naming conventions to exported files for easier import and organization.
Applies a bias to the land color or contour mapping, shifting emphasis to certain elevation ranges or features.
Applies a bias to the water color or contour mapping, shifting emphasis to certain depth ranges or features.
Applies a directional or environmental bias to shrub placement, favoring certain areas or conditions.
Applies a secondary shaping function or modifier, allowing for additional variation and detail in the ice floes.
Applies a shaping function to modify the curve of values.
Applies a skew or bias to the distance field, distorting the propagation direction for creative or technical effects.
Applies additional enhancement to the gradient's tonal range or contrast before tinting.
Applies additional enhancement to the texture's tonal range or contrast.
Applies additional random displacement to the warp, increasing the irregularity and complexity of the effect.
Applies an angular tilt to the sandstone layers, simulating geological tilting or shifting of strata.
Applies an angular tilt to the stratified layers, simulating geological tilting or shifting of strata.
Applies an erosion effect to the map, softening features and simulating natural terrain wear.
Applies antialiasing to the slope blur effect, reducing jagged edges and improving visual smoothness.
Applies antialiasing to the slope warp effect, reducing jagged edges and improving visual smoothness.
Applies custom influence maps or masks to control tree placement according to user specifications, enabling highly tailored results.
Applies directional scaling to the fractal, stretching or compressing features along a specific axis.
Applies distortion to the plate boundaries, introducing irregularity and natural variation to the shapes.
Applies erosion to the coastal areas where the sea meets the land, simulating natural shoreline wear and shaping.
Applies finer warping to add small-scale distortion and surface complexity without changing the overall canyon layout.
Applies large-scale warping to the canyon structure to introduce bends, meanders, and macro variation.
Applies post-processing to reduce visual artifacts in the mesh, such as smoothing or correcting problematic geometry.
Applies random offset to cell positions along the X axis, introducing irregularity and breaking uniformity.
Applies random offset to cell positions along the Y axis, adding variation and natural randomness.
Applies random offset to cell positions along the Z axis, further enhancing the organic appearance of the 3D pattern.
Applies random or specified rotation to each outcrop, increasing natural variation and preventing repetitive patterns.
Applies the first shaping function or modifier to the ice floes, affecting their outline and internal structure.
Applies uniform scaling to all axes, maintaining the original proportions of the terrain or object.
Automatically adjusts the levels of each RGB channel independently, ensuring optimal contrast and brightness for each channel after splitting.
Automatically adjusts the levels of the combined channels to maximize the output range.
Automatically adjusts values to span the full output range.
Automatically crops the loaded file to a square aspect ratio, which is often required for terrain processing.
